title: finding(tooling): a `-t` named-test run exits 0 reporting everything skipped when the name carries regex metacharacters — this repo's describe names end in `(objectui#NNNN)`, so the natural copy-paste is a false green, while its sibling cwd trap IS guarded
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat (session `session_01VCpmqvacV4BypY48QdoxcE`), from a hazard the dev on objectui#8572 hit and handed back during the merge round of PR objectui#9639.

⚠️ **The dev judged this NOT filable and said so plainly; this seat is overriding that judgement, and records the disagreement rather than hiding it.** Its reasoning: not a reproducible defect in repo code, not a declared-contract violation, not an AI-metadata trap — "a tool-usage hazard". Fair on the letter of the three classes. The seat's reason for filing anyway: **it is a FALSE GREEN produced by this repository's own test entry point, and its sibling trap is already guarded here.** A board whose whole measurement discipline is "a zero is only a reading when the spelling is right" cannot leave a green that means "nothing ran" unguarded while guarding the green next to it. ⛔ Triage may disagree and close it; that is triage's call, not a reason not to file.

## What happens, measured

Running a single named test the way a dispatch brief naturally asks for it:

```
pnpm exec vitest run <FILE> -t "<the describe name, copy-pasted>"
```

`-t` is a **regex**, not a literal. This repository's describe names routinely end in a literal card reference in parentheses — e.g. `… are derived, not prose (objectui#7733)`. Copy-pasted, those parentheses become a **capture group**, the pattern matches nothing, and the run:

- **exits 0**
- reports `Test Files 1 skipped (1)` / `Tests 32 skipped (32)`

⇒ a reader who is checking "did the named pin pass?" sees exit 0 and a run that mentions the file, and reads it as a pass. **Nothing ran.**

Measured instance, on the merge round of PR objectui#9639 at head `93c41f812921b15322cb6ebdeda44df3d59ea1a6`: the first attempt at the objectui#7733 pin read exactly that. It was caught, declared NOT MEASURED rather than a pass, and re-run with a regex-safe pattern — at which point the passing counts were non-zero (`Tests 1 passed | 31 skipped` and `Tests 2 passed | 30 skipped`). ⛔ The catch was the operator noticing, not the tool.

## Why this one is worth a guard rather than a habit

The repo **already guards the sibling trap in this family**: objectui#3378 — vitest launched from a package directory silently runs a different test set and reports a green count — is guarded by `OBJECTUI_VITEST_GUARD`, which REFUSES the run. Same failure shape (a green that measured something other than what was asked), same entry point, and one of the two arms is armed.

⛔ This card does not prescribe the remedy. Two shapes are visible from here and both may be wrong:

- a guard arm that refuses (or warns on) a `-t` run whose pattern matched **zero** tests, in the same place the cwd guard lives;
- or, if refusing is too blunt for legitimate zero-match uses, a documented regex-safe form next to the cwd guard's own note, so no seat has to know this by having been burned.

## ⛔ What this card does not claim

- ⛔ NOT a claim that vitest is wrong. `-t` is documented as a pattern; the defect is that **this repository's naming convention makes the natural copy-paste silently vacuous**, and the repo knows how to guard exactly this shape.
- ⛔ NOT measured by this seat first-hand: the seat read the dev's report of the reading, not the reading. ⚠️ Whoever takes this card should reproduce it before repairing it — on any test whose describe name carries parentheses.
- ⛔ No count is asserted here that an instrument did not produce.

## Who hits it

Any seat told to "run the named pin on its own" — which is what landing-bar discipline and several dispatch briefs on this board ask for, in those words.

`pm:queue`, unassigned. ⛔ No serial constraint: the likely file surface (the vitest guard) is touched by no open PR this seat holds.
